_about: Delivery targets and on-screen safe zones per platform at a 1080x1920 canvas. qa-reel.py, finish-reel.py and render-reel.py read this file. Safe-zone numbers are pixels from that edge that platform UI may cover; captions, cover text and supers stay OUT of those bands. Sources, dates checked, and the reasoning behind every number live in platform-specs.md beside this file. When two platforms are targeted, the strictest value wins (largest band, shortest max duration).

instagram_reels.safe_zone_note: Meta 2026 unified 9:16 guidance: 14% top, 35% bottom, 6% each side.

youtube_shorts.safe_zone_note: Title and channel row at the bottom, action rail on the right. Practitioner consensus, no official pixel spec.

tiktok.safe_zone_note: TikTok creative best practices: keep key elements clear of the top status area, the bottom caption and audio strip, and the right action rail.

facebook_reels.safe_zone_note: Same unified Meta 9:16 guidance as Instagram Reels.

loudness_pipeline.note: The pipeline masters to -16 LUFS integrated, -1.5 dBTP, and keeps LRA=11 in the loudnorm target because linear (two-pass) mode silently reverts to dynamic when the measured LRA exceeds the target LRA. Platforms then normalize toward about -14 LUFS themselves. QA compares the delivered file to the manifest target when one is given. Loudness Range is informational only: EBU R128 s1 states LRA limits do not apply to short-form programmes.

captions.note: Netflix timing guidelines: 20-frame minimum event, 2-frame minimum gap, 20 characters per second for adults, 42 characters per line on a 16:9 frame. A 1080-wide vertical frame at caption size 42 to 48 fits about 32 characters per line inside the side safe zones.
